# CoreWeave filings, read Wed Nov 25, 18:16 ET

| Item | Figure | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Debt principal due | rest of 2026 **$2,433M**; 2027 **$10,974M**; 2028 $5,479M; 2029 $4,727M; 2030 $4,247M; after $19,645M; total **$47,505M** | 10-Q for Sep 30, 2026, Note 10 table (accession 0001769628-26-000465, filed 2026-11-12), read at sec.gov |
| Covenants | 'As of September 30, 2026, the Company was in compliance with all covenants under its loan agreements' | same |
| Cash | cash and equivalents $4,122M; restricted cash $1,405M current, $877M non-current; undrawn facilities $5.7B | same |
| Interest | contractual interest $766M in Q3 (Q3 2025 $324M) | same |
| Leases due 2027 | operating $2,375M, finance $361M (not debt) | same |
| Company view | cash and facilities 'will be sufficient' for obligations due within one year of the filing | same, management's statement |
| EDGAR since the 10-Q | Form 4s and 144s only; last 8-K 2026-11-10 (Items 2.02, 9.01). No Item 1.03 (bankruptcy) or 2.04 (acceleration) filing | data.sec.gov submissions, read 18:16 ET |

- **Corrects nothing on the BOARD; confirms an earlier figure:** WALTER's earlier $11.0 billion due in 2027 (from a page citing the 10-Q) is right at the filing: $10.974B. The bookmark's '$13.5 billion owed next year' stays unsupported; debt plus 2027 lease payments is $13.71B, a different measure.
- **Limits:** a Sep 30 snapshot, before the November bond moves and the $4.5B Meta-backed loan (not launched as last read, card 035). An 8-K can be filed after this read; a filing absence is not a credit judgement.
- **So what:** about $13.4B of principal falls due in the 15 months to end-2027, against $4.1B unrestricted cash and $5.7B undrawn at Sep 30, so refinancing access matters; how much of 2027 is scheduled amortization on asset-backed loans versus a single maturity is not in this table. LIQUID, BROCK and VULCAN own the read; TERRY holds the approved NOT-FIRED CRWV idea (WQ-745).

# Co-movement test, CoreWeave, Oracle, Arm, SoftBank

| Pair | Oct 12 to Nov 24 (32 sessions) | Jul 1 to Oct 9 | Same, after removing SPY and SMH |
|---|---|---|---|
| CRWV-ORCL | 0.88 | 0.63 | 0.65 (was 0.46) |
| CRWV-ARM | 0.89 | 0.50 | 0.55 (was -0.10) |
| ORCL-ARM | 0.83 | 0.51 | 0.36 (was 0.12) |
| SoftBank next Tokyo session vs ORCL, CRWV, ARM, SMH | 0.39, 0.38, 0.40, 0.38 | 0.33 to 0.45 | not computed |

Daily returns, vendor closes; WALTER arithmetic, not a desk grade. Arm stands in as a SoftBank-held US listing.

**Documented links (desk records, in CONNECTIONS.md):** SoftBank to OpenAI (about $64.6B; a $10B loan against OpenAI shares with a value-linked prepayment, threshold undisclosed; KB-SAM-261, KB-VULCAN-404); Oracle to OpenAI (S&P 7/9 'key credit risk'; share of backlog 45 to 54% is relay-grade; KB-VULCAN-401); CoreWeave to OpenAI listed as backlog exposure, not sized (KB-178). No SoftBank to Oracle credit tie (SAM 11/06).

**The question for the owners:** is the rise in co-movement an OpenAI-specific chain (weaker confidence in OpenAI's payments lowers its value, pressuring SoftBank's loan and Oracle's backlog) or one broad AI-financing selloff? WALTER's data cannot separate them. **Tells:** OpenAI-specific news hitting Oracle and SoftBank but not the rest of AI; or a prepayment, gate or pulled deal naming two of the names. **Against contagion:** CoreWeave's Meta-backed loan is drawing interest (card 035); BROCK's named private-credit exposures to AI cloud firms are each under 1% of their funds.

- **Limits:** 32 sessions is short; returns overlap one selloff; the residual removes only SPY and SMH; the SoftBank lag test uses Tokyo closes after the US session.
- **Ask:** SAM (SoftBank, OpenAI loan) and VULCAN (Oracle, CoreWeave, OpenAI backlog) say whether this is worth a desk test, and if so own it. A 'no' is a complete answer. TERRY by BOARD.
